accepted.s: The seals of the Indus Valley Civilization were made mostly of which material?
accepted.x: Most Indus seals were made of steatite, or soapstone, because it was easy to carve. Terracotta, copper and ivory were also used.
accepted.tq: Use the material clue and distinguish the predominant material from occasional alternatives.
accepted.sec: Seals and sealings - material, shapes, uses, value as the main source  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the shapes and designs of Harappan seals:
1. Square seals generally carry an animal figure along with an inscription.
2. Rectangular seals generally carry only an inscription.
3. Mesopotamian-type cylinder seals were common at all Harappan sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Square seals commonly show an animal and inscription, whereas rectangular seals generally carry only an inscription. Mesopotamian-type cylinder seals were rare, not common.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong statement by checking the frequency qualifier in statement 3.
accepted.sec: Seals and sealings - material, shapes, uses, value as the main source  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A button seal associated with the Harappan Civilization has been found at:
accepted.x: A button seal is specifically associated with Lothal.
accepted.tq: Test the site associated with a distinctive seal type.
accepted.sec: Seals and sealings - material, shapes, uses, value as the main source  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the principal purpose of stamping wet clay on the closed bags of goods in the Harappan period?
o: To indicate safe delivery and ownership
To identify the metal content of the goods
To mark the burial place of the owner
accepted.x: Bags of goods were closed with wet clay and stamped. An intact sealing on arrival indicated safe delivery and ownership.
accepted.tq: Apply the function of sealing to a trade-and-transport situation.
accepted.sec: Seals and sealings - material, shapes, uses, value as the main source  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a recognized function associated with Harappan seals and sealings?
accepted.x: Seals could indicate identity, regulate trade and facilitate long-distance communication. They have not led to the decipherment of the Harappan script.
accepted.tq: Find the option that describes an unrelated result rather than a function.
accepted.sec: Seals and sealings - material, shapes, uses, value as the main source  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The most distinctive artefact and a key source for studying the people of the Indus Valley Civilization, in the absence of a deciphered script, is the:
accepted.x: Since the Harappan script remains unread, seals are regarded as the most distinctive artefacts and an important source of information about Harappan society.
accepted.tq: Link the absence of decipherment with the principal archaeological source.
accepted.sec: Seals and sealings - material, shapes, uses, value as the main source  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Scale)
A. Ivory scale
B. Shell scale
C. Copper scale

List-II (Site)
1. Lothal
2. Mohenjodaro
3. Harappa

A B C
(a) 1 2 3
(b) 2 3 1
(c) 3 1 2
(d) 1 3 2
accepted.x: The ivory scale was found at Lothal, the shell scale at Mohenjodaro and the copper scale at Harappa.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of the ivory scale and eliminate mismatched site combinations.
accepted.sec: Measures - scale finds → site + material, unit length  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The scale divided into units of approximately 1.75 cm, referred to as an “inch” in the Harappan measurement system, is associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: The 1.75 cm division was a linear unit of the Harappan measurement system and was described as an “inch”.
accepted.tq: Identify the physical quantity represented by the stated unit length.
accepted.sec: Measures - scale finds → site + material, unit length  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets correctly represents the approximate Harappan units of length?
accepted.x: The Harappan foot was about 37.6 cm, while the cubit was approximately 51.8–53.6 cm.
accepted.tq: Separate the related numerical units by their relative magnitude.
accepted.sec: Measures - scale finds → site + material, unit length  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A shell instrument probably used for measuring angles has been reported from:
accepted.x: A shell instrument believed to have been used for measuring angles was found at Lothal in the Saurashtra region.
accepted.tq: Associate the unusual instrument with its specific site and region.
accepted.sec: Measures - scale finds → site + material, unit length  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about animals represented in Harappan art:
1. The unicorn is the most common animal motif on seals.
2. Cow and lion are absent from Harappan seals.
3. The horse figure is reported from Lothal terracotta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The unicorn is the most common seal motif; cow and lion are absent from seals; and a horse figure has been reported from Lothal terracotta.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the separate seal and terracotta distributions.
accepted.sec: Animals depicted and not depicted on seals and terracotta  [other exams]

accepted.s: The great humpless bull figurines are particularly associated with Harappan:
accepted.x: Great humpless bull figurines are noted among Harappan terracotta objects.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive animal figurine with its material category.
accepted.sec: Animals depicted and not depicted on seals and terracotta  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Cylindrical seal with alligator motif — Lothal
accepted.x: The Pashupati seal, showing a seated yogic figure surrounded by animals, was found at Mohenjodaro. The Persian Gulf-type and button seals are associated with Lothal.
accepted.tq: Use site-specific seal associations and reject swapped locations.

accepted.s: The famous bull seal of the Harappan Civilization was found at:
accepted.x: The famous bull seal is associated with Mohenjodaro.
accepted.tq: Recall the site of a named famous seal rather than the general seal distribution.

accepted.s: A cylindrical steatite seal bearing an alligator motif and five characters has been reported from:
accepted.x: A cylindrical steatite seal with an alligator motif and five Harappan characters was reported from Rakhigarhi.
accepted.tq: Identify the site from a distinctive motif-and-inscription combination.

accepted.s:
Harappan seals have been found outside the Indian subcontinent at which of the following places?
1. Susa
2. Ur
3. Nippur
4. Failaka and Bahrain
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Harappan seals have been found at Susa, Ur, Nippur, Failaka and Bahrain, indicating wide-ranging external contacts.
accepted.tq: Treat the list as cumulative and verify whether every named overseas location belongs.

accepted.s: Harappan weights were generally made of:
o: Chert and, in some cases, limestone and steatite
accepted.x: Harappan weights were mostly made of chert, with limestone and steatite also used.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the dominant material from materials used for scales or balances.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the usual shape of Harappan weights?
accepted.x: Harappan weights were generally cubical in shape.
accepted.tq: Test the standard physical form of the object directly.

accepted.s: The numerical system of Harappan weights is best represented by:
o: A sexagesimal system without binary subdivisions
Only a decimal system from the smallest denomination onward
A random system varying from site to site
Binary values in lower denominations followed by decimal multiples
accepted.x: Lower denominations followed the binary sequence 1:2:4:8:16:32:64, after which decimal multiples such as 160, 320 and 640 were used.
accepted.tq: Separate the two successive numerical principles instead of treating the system as uniform.

accepted.s: Which one of the following represents the binary sequence used in the lower denominations of Harappan weights?
accepted.x: The lower denominations followed the binary progression 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64.
accepted.tq: Recognize the doubling pattern in the numerical sequence.

accepted.s: The approximate standard unit represented by the Harappan “16” weight was:
accepted.x: The Harappan “16” weight represented a standard unit of approximately 13.63 grams.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the weight value from the separate linear units in the measurement system.

accepted.s: The discovery of essentially similar weights across an area of about 8,00,000 square kilometres indicates:
o: Independent measurement systems at every site
Exclusive use of weights for religious rituals
accepted.x: The distribution of similar weights over about 8,00,000 square kilometres suggests central regulation and standardized trade practices.
accepted.tq: Infer administrative and economic organization from uniform material standards.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Ivory weight balance — Mohenjodaro and Lothal
2. Chert trade weights — Rakhigarhi
3. Cubical weights — Harappan measurement system
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Ivory weight balances are associated with Mohenjodaro and Lothal, chert trade weights have been reported from Rakhigarhi, and Harappan weights were generally cubical.
accepted.tq: Combine material, site and shape clues without confusing balances with the weights themselves.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Harappan script is correct?
o: It is fully deciphered and consists only of numerical symbols.
It is mostly pictographic, with some abstract signs, and the fish is the most common sign.
It is entirely alphabetic and contains no pictographic signs.
It is exclusively composed of animal images without abstract signs.
accepted.x: The Harappan script is mostly pictographic but also contains abstract signs. The fish is reported as the most common sign.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute descriptions such as “entirely” and “exclusively” when the script has mixed features.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - direction, decipherment status, number of signs, pictographic nature

accepted.s: The usual direction of writing in the Harappan script is:
accepted.x: Harappan inscriptions were generally written from right to left, as indicated partly by cramped spacing at the left end.
accepted.tq: Use the directional clue associated with the spacing of signs.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - direction, decipherment status, number of signs, pictographic nature

accepted.s: Boustrophedon writing in the Harappan context refers to:
o: Writing from the centre towards both margins
Writing with symbols arranged in circles
Writing in alternate lines in opposite directions
accepted.x: Boustrophedon writing means that alternate lines run in opposite directions. This pattern is associated, for example, with Kalibangan.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the technical term by its directional meaning rather than by the writing material.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - direction, decipherment status, number of signs, pictographic nature

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the number of signs in the Harappan script is correct?
o: The script contains fewer than 50 signs according to all estimates.
Estimates range from about 400 to 700 signs, with about 400 often cited.
The script contains more than 5,000 distinct signs.
The script contains exactly 26 signs like the English alphabet.
accepted.x: Estimates of the number of Harappan signs range from about 400 to 700, while around 400 signs are commonly cited.
accepted.tq: Handle a range and a commonly cited estimate without treating them as contradictory.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - direction, decipherment status, number of signs, pictographic nature

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan inscriptions:
1. The average inscription contains about five signs.
2. Around 5,000 inscribed objects are known.
3. A bilingual inscription has enabled the script to be conclusively deciphered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The average inscription has about five signs and approximately 5,000 inscribed objects are known. No bilingual text has been found, so the script remains undeciphered.
accepted.tq: Identify the false statement by testing the claimed basis for decipherment.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - direction, decipherment status, number of signs, pictographic nature

accepted.s:
The Harappan script has been found on which of the following objects?
1. Seals and tablets
2. Pottery and copper plates
3. Tools
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Harappan signs occur on seals, tablets, pottery, copper plates and tools. Therefore, all three groups are correct.
accepted.tq: Check whether each group belongs to the recorded media of inscription.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - direction, decipherment status, number of signs, pictographic nature

accepted.s: Who noticed seals bearing unknown symbols in 1912?
accepted.x: J. Fleet noticed seals with unknown symbols in 1912.
accepted.tq: Link the early observation to the scholar and year rather than to later decipherment proposals.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - direction, decipherment status, number of signs, pictographic nature

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

List-I (Hypothesis)
A. Proto-Dravidian
B. Indo-Aryan or early Sanskrit
C. Proto-Munda
D. Isolate

List-II (Associated scholar or position)
1. S.R. Rao
2. Iravatham Mahadevan and Asko Parpola
3. Weak linguistic support
4. Decipherment considered impossible for now

A B C D
(a) 2 1 3 4
(b) 1 2 3 4
(c) 2 1 4 3
(d) 3 1 2 4
accepted.x: The Proto-Dravidian hypothesis is associated with Iravatham Mahadevan and Asko Parpola; the Indo-Aryan view with S.R. Rao; Proto-Munda has weak linguistic support; and the isolate view considers decipherment impossible for now.
accepted.tq: Start with the scholar–hypothesis pair and then match the two positions by their wording.

accepted.s: Which hypothesis regarding the Harappan script is currently the most widely supported?
accepted.x: The Proto-Dravidian interpretation, associated with Iravatham Mahadevan and Asko Parpola, is the most widely supported hypothesis.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the prevailing hypothesis from minority and non-linguistic positions.

accepted.s: The Indo-Aryan or early Sanskrit interpretation of the Harappan script is associated with:
accepted.x: S.R. Rao proposed the Indo-Aryan or early Sanskrit interpretation, which remains a minority view.
accepted.tq: Use the scholar–hypothesis association and avoid substituting a Proto-Dravidian proponent.

accepted.s: The longest known Harappan inscription contains:
accepted.x: The longest known Harappan inscription consists of 26 signs.
accepted.tq: Separate the general sign count from the length of the longest individual inscription.

accepted.s: The famous Dholavira signboard contains:
accepted.x: The Dholavira signboard is famous for its inscription of 10 large signs.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ten-sign signboard from the 26-sign longest inscription.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events or associations in chronological order:
A. Excavation of Dholavira by R.S. Bisht
B. J. Fleet notices seals with unknown symbols
C. Dholavira is included on the UNESCO World Heritage List
D. Report of the Rakhigarhi alligator-motif seal

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: J. Fleet noticed the unknown symbols in 1912; Dholavira was excavated by R.S. Bisht in 1990; it entered the UNESCO list in 2021; and the Rakhigarhi report belongs to the later 2026 reporting context.
accepted.tq: Fix the early dated event first, then place the excavation, UNESCO listing and recent report.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Dholavira is correct?
o: It was excavated by R.S. Bisht in 1990 and is the only Harappan site on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
It was excavated by J. Fleet in 1912 and is on the Tentative List only.
It is the only Harappan site located outside the Indian subcontinent.
It was excavated by S.R. Rao in 2021 and has no UNESCO recognition.
accepted.x: Dholavira was excavated by R.S. Bisht in 1990 and is the only Harappan site on the UNESCO World Heritage List, having been listed in 2021.
accepted.tq: Combine the excavator, year and heritage-status clues while rejecting swapped authorities.

accepted.s: Which Harappan site is on the Tentative List rather than the UNESCO World Heritage List?
accepted.x: Rakhigarhi is on the Tentative List, whereas Dholavira is the only Harappan site on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the World Heritage List and the Tentative List status.

accepted.s: The presence of uniform seals and weights across the Harappan cultural region is the main evidence for:
accepted.x: Uniform seals and weights indicate standardisation and regulated trade across the Harappan cultural region.
accepted.tq: Infer the wider institutional meaning from archaeological uniformity.

accepted.s: Which issue concerning the Harappan script remains open?
o: Whether Harappan weights were cubical or spherical
Whether its language was Dravidian or Indo-Aryan
Whether Dholavira was a Harappan site
Whether seals were made of steatite or iron
accepted.x: The language underlying the undeciphered script remains debated, particularly between Dravidian and Indo-Aryan interpretations.
accepted.tq: Identify the unresolved linguistic debate rather than settled archaeological facts.

accepted.s: The Indus script is regarded as:
o: A medieval alphabet developed after the Gupta period
The earliest fully deciphered script in the world
A purely modern system of commercial symbols
Among the world’s earliest writing systems
accepted.x: The Indus script is considered one of the world’s earliest writing systems, although it remains undeciphered.
accepted.tq: Separate antiquity from decipherment status and reject the overstatement of complete decipherment.
